questions.question: Explain the characteristics of transition metals with reference to electronic configuration, variable oxidation states and colour.
questions.solution:
Transition metals have an incompletely filled (n−1)d subshell in the atom or in a common oxidation state — e.g. Fe: [Ar]3d⁶4s².

**Variable oxidation states:** the 3d and 4s energies are close, so both sets of electrons can be lost; oxidation states differ by 1 (Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺, Mn²⁺ to Mn⁷⁺).

**Colour:** in an octahedral field the d orbitals split, and d–d transitions absorb visible light, giving coloured ions (Cu²⁺ blue, Fe³⁺ yellow-brown). Ions with d⁰ or d¹⁰ have no d–d transition: Zn²⁺ and Sc³⁺ are colourless.

**Other features:** catalytic activity (Fe in Haber, V₂O₅ in contact process) and paramagnetism from unpaired electrons.
questions.knowledgeNote: Zn is a transition element structurally but not typically classed as one chemically, since Zn²⁺ is d¹⁰ (no variable states, no colour).

questions.question: Describe the general principles of extraction of metals from their oxide ores with examples of the reducing agents used.
questions.knowledgeNote: The Ellingham diagram formalises this: a reducing agent will reduce only those oxides whose formation free energy is lower on the plot — hence carbon above 983 K for iron.

questions.question: What are lanthanoid contraction and its consequences? Write one use of a lanthanoid.
questions.solution:
**Lanthanoid contraction** is the steady decrease in atomic and ionic radii from La to Lu, caused by the poor shielding of the increasing nuclear charge by the 4f electrons.

**Consequences:** (i) Zr and Hf resemble each other so closely that their separation is difficult; (ii) the basicity of the hydroxides decreases steadily across the series; (iii) the lanthanoids themselves show very similar chemical properties, making separation (usually by ion exchange) a demanding process.

**Use:** mischmetal (alloy of lanthanoids) in lighter flints; Gd and other lanthanoids in phosphors and magnets.
questions.knowledgeNote: 4f electrons shield the nuclear charge badly because their shape is diffuse — the same reason the 5d electrons are pulled in, explaining the transactinide behaviour.
